correctness.rationale: The lower flight leaves the positive section first. Involutivity of the lower map gives r_(n+1)-r_n=chi(s_n), with s_n=-r_n+O(r_n^2); the even mismatch order gives the stated sign and coefficient. With q=2p-1, the reciprocal-power increment is qc+O(r_n), which gives n r_n^q -> 1/(qc). Along each half-flight, horizontal motion is monotone, its length is 2r_n+O(r_n^2), and dy/dx=O(|x|+|y|) bounds the height by O(r_n^2). The reciprocal horizontal speeds thus integrate to a full clock increment K r_n+O(r_n^2), with the absolute value on b_-. For q>1, summing the clock gives t_n r_n^(q-1) -> K/[c(q-1)]. For q=1, the increments of log r_n+(c/K)t_n are O(r_n^2); these are summable, proving a finite real log limit and hence a strictly positive finite prefactor. The polynomial example has lower return -r and upper first integral y+x^2+c x^(2p+1); its upper return equation gives the coefficient -c for every p. These arguments concern positive crossings and original time, not signed position between crossings.
